headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: gpt-researcher can ingest local documents and broad network content, while unstructured can write processed outputs that may be reused without verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-researcher ingests browser/web content and local documents, and unstructured processes documents into text. If gpt-researcher’s outputs are fed into unstructured or vice versa through a shared workspace, attacker-controlled content can influence downstream instructions. The pair has no documented provenance tracking, so the interaction is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF the two agents exchange files through a shared workspace or pipeline
IF either agent treats extracted document text as instructions
mitigations: Separate input and output directories per agent
Add a provenance header to every intermediate file
Require manual review before re-feeding outputs
Disable automatic re-ingestion of generated documents

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-researcher touches local documents and multiple API keys, while unstructured reads and writes documents in a containerized pipeline. If they share a workspace, sensitive document contents can flow from A into B’s outputs or logs. This is not critical because neither profile shows uncontrolled third-party exfiltration of the full context window, but the shared-document pathway is credible.
conditions: IF both agents can access the same document directory
IF processed outputs are stored alongside source documents
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for source and derived files
Turn off verbose logging for both agents
Delete intermediate artifacts after each run

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can read the filesystem, install packages, and spawn subprocesses; unstructured can also write the filesystem. In a shared directory, concurrent runs can overwrite inputs, outputs, or dependency state, and gpt-researcher’s multiple-instance support increases collision risk. The overlap is dangerous by default if orchestrated together without locks.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same writable directory
IF runs occur concurrently without file locking
mitigations: Serialize writes with a lock file
Mount shared data read-only where possible

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher produces research reports and citations, and unstructured can transform documents that may be consumed downstream. If unstructured treats gpt-researcher’s output as authoritative, errors or hallucinated citations can cascade into later document processing. The pair lacks an explicit verification step in the profiles, so the risk exists in default orchestration but is not inherently irreversible.
conditions: IF unstructured ingests gpt-researcher reports without validation
IF downstream users rely on the transformed output as factual
mitigations: Insert a verification step between agents
Keep human review for final publication

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch stated. gpt-researcher handles API keys and research documents, while unstructured processes documents in a container, but the profiles do not show a concrete compliance conflict. Because the evidence is sparse, I avoid asserting a stronger mismatch.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through a non-compliant deployment of either agent
IF retention policies differ in the surrounding infrastructure
mitigations: Set retention limits in the orchestrator
Avoid regulated data until policies are documented
